dod_intent_evidence: Two DOD Phase II SBIR awards under their own name — Army 2023 'Next Generation Network Mapping' ($1,698,226) and USAF 2025 'Automated Cyber Defense for the USAF Network' ($1,237,484) — per SBIR.gov records and their own press release.
score_evidence: 'Cyber Fundamentals, Delivered At Machine Speed' / 'Every IP address is inspected on all 65,535 ports' → lab_language_intensity

'There is zero deployment and no effort needed from the customer... you provide us with your company name—and only your company name' → deployment_awareness_absence (no ATO/RMF/DDIL framing at all despite a live USAF network-defense SBIR)
Personas listed are exclusively 'CISO / SOC / Network / IT / GRC' → operator_absence (no operators, warfighters, training, or CONOPS anywhere)
Open roles: 4x 'Senior Customer Success Manager,' zero field/deployment/compliance/ISSO roles despite the active USAF Phase II award → hiring_profile_skew

blind_spots.blind_spot: The platform's entire onboarding promise is 'zero deployment' — you give SixMap your company name and it scans the public internet for you.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A USAF network-defense SBIR implies exposure assessment against segmented, classified, or air-gapped DoD network enclaves that don't present themselves to internet-facing recon the way a corporate cloud tenant does — the product's core method (external scan, no agent, no on-network footprint) may simply return nothing for the segments that actually need protecting.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product was built and proven against commercial enterprise attack surfaces (Fortune 500, financial services) where 'no deployment' is the selling point; the team hasn't yet had to explain that promise against a DDIL or classified DoD boundary.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: There is zero deployment and no effort needed from the customer.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Marketing claims comprehensive discovery 'across IPv4 and IPv6' and inspection of 'all 65,535 ports' on every host with zero mention of ATO/RMF, IL4/IL5, or CMMC for the platform itself.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Running continuous external reconnaissance against a USAF network as a SaaS vendor requires its own authorization boundary and likely classification handling — without ATO/RMF language, there's no visible plan for how SixMap itself gets authorized to touch what it's scanning.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The SBIR is fresh (Phase II awarded 2025) and the public-facing site still speaks entirely in commercial cyber-vendor language.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Every IP address is inspected on all 65,535 ports and every domain is thoroughly assessed to uncover all exposures across your environment.

blind_spots.blind_spot: All four open roles are Customer Success Manager positions — none are field, compliance, ISSO, or deployment engineering roles.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A company actively executing a $1.24M USAF Phase II SBIR for network cyber defense is hiring exclusively for post-sale commercial account management, not for the accreditation/compliance/field-integration work a DoD network rollout requires — suggesting the SBIR deliverable and the commercial go-to-market are on separate tracks with no headcount bridging them.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Series A stage-pressure is pushing hiring toward proving commercial ARR (CS headcount) rather than DoD-specific deployment capability.

opener_hook: SixMap's Phase II USAF SBIR ($1.24M, awarded 2025) funds 'Automated Cyber Defense for the USAF Network' — the platform's listed onboarding step is 'you provide us with your company name, and only your company name.'
what_they_do: External attack-surface / preemptive exposure management SaaS (IPv4/IPv6 network discovery and vulnerability prioritization) sold to commercial CISOs and public-sector agencies, now adapting the platform to USAF network cyber defense under SBIR.
